steps.body: Write how many, teen edition: claim the full ten at sight, count on the extras, and write both pieces — 1 then the extras' digit.
steps.narration: Write how many, teen edition: claim the full ten at sight, count on the extras, and write both pieces — 1 then the extras' digit.

widget.prompt: Seventeen is a full ten plus 7 more. Tap 7 dots to show the 'more' part.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 7 dots still missing. Continue until the frame shows exactly 7.
6 leaves 1 dot still missing. Continue until the frame shows exactly 7.
8 adds 1 too many. Remove the extra so the frame shows exactly 7.

widget.missFeedback: Tap the dots one at a time. Stop when the frame shows exactly 7 — that's the 'more' part of 17.
widget.successFeedback: Ten and 7 — the numeral 17 writes those two pieces side by side.

predict.prompt: Seventeen is a full ten plus 7 loose dots. The numeral you write is…
predict.reveal: The frame's ten belongs in the numeral too — the leading 1 records it.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write count teens.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write count teens.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: One full ten and three extra dots need a numeral label. Which one?

options.feedback: 14 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 13.
12 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 13.

hotspots.feedback: One ten and seven ones are written 17.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 7. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 16 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 17.
18 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 7 hops from 10 to land on 17.

widget.missFeedback: Count 7 on from 10: you land on 17.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 7 more is 17 — the teen numeral writes exactly that: 1 ten, 7 ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 7 counts past ten are needed to reach 17.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 7 numbers, on 17.

widget.prompt: Kai counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: The count stopped at 9; writing one more would record a block that is not there.
That records one too few — the count reached 9, so the numeral must too.
That runs two past the count; the written numeral copies the last word said, 9.
Correct — the last number said, 9, is the one the numeral must record.
